## The issue

**#48 — Land card resets the squash/merge choice after every other button on it** — https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/48

Do this issue and nothing else. Do not fix other defects you notice — note them in your final report instead.

## Setup — do this first, and abort loudly if it fails

    export GH_PAGER=cat
    gh auth status
    REPO=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner)

Pass `--repo "$REPO"` on every subsequent `gh` call rather than relying on the inferred remote. Read the comments as well as the body. If the issue is already closed, stop and report that rather than implementing it a second time.

Read `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` before touching anything. This repository documents its reasoning at length and several things that look like bugs are deliberate and explained there — in particular the whole of `land.ts`'s design, since landing is a write into the operator's own checkout with no undo.

## What to do

In `src/components/RunLand.tsx`: `load()` ends by overwriting the operator's landing strategy with the server default (`:201`, `setStrategy(res.data.defaultStrategy)` — unconditional), and `act()` calls `load()` after **every** action on the card (`:218-247`). So pressing Commit, Delete, Purge or Resolve — or a Land that failed and whose refusal has since cleared — silently resets the select, and the next press of Land does something the operator explicitly chose against. `defaultStrategy` is `getSettings().landStrategy` (`src/app/api/runs/[id]/land/route.ts:40`), which ships as `"merge"`, so the choice discarded is always **Squash into one commit**.

The reachable path is routine, not a corner case: a branch with commits **and** uncommitted work in its checkout shows the strategy select and the Commit control at the same time, so the operator picks Squash, presses Commit first because the card tells them to, and the select snaps back to Merge under them.

Seed from the server only while the operator has not chosen — the issue body carries a suggested shape (`setStrategy((s) => s ?? res.data.defaultStrategy)` with the state widened to nullable). Verify it against the real code rather than pasting it. Whichever shape you take, make sure the **value displayed in the select and the value sent in `act`** cannot part company: render the select from the same fallback expression that `act` sends, so there is one source of truth for what pressing Land will do.

Check the same pattern is not repeated for the card's other server-seeded controls, and if it is, fix only the ones that carry an operator's choice into a write — say what you found either way.

Add a regression test if one can be written without inventing new harness machinery for this file; `src/components/Meter.test.tsx`, `LiveTelemetry.test.tsx` and `Markdown.test.tsx` are the precedent for a rendering test in this repository, and `CLAUDE.md` records the bar such a test has to clear. If a test for this component would need machinery that does not exist here, say so plainly in your report and in the closing comment rather than adding a framework.

**Fixed and closed.** `src/components/RunLand.tsx`, committed as `e648eef` on `uf/usagefoundry-5-7c219726` — not merged to main.

**The change.** The one `strategy` variable held two facts, so it is now two: `strategy` (`:178`) is `MergeStrategyDTO | null`, null until the select is touched, written only by the select's `onChange` (`:524`); `defaultStrategy` (`:179`) holds the server's answer, and `load()` refreshes it freely at `:219` where the unconditional `setStrategy(res.data.defaultStrategy)` used to be. `MergeStrategyDTO` (`src/lib/apiTypes.ts:501`) replaces the three inline unions.

**Displayed vs sent.** `const effectiveStrategy = strategy ?? defaultStrategy` (`:194`) is a single local with exactly three readers, all moved onto it: the select's `value` (`:523`), `act`'s POST body (`:248`), and the "a squash rewrites the commits" sentence above the button (`:501`). `strategy` is read nowhere else in the file, so the value on screen and the value on the wire are the same binding from the same render. The third reader had to move too — it describes what the button will do.

**Other server-seeded controls on the card:** none. `state`/`resolution`/`readError` are server data with no choice in them, `confirmPurge` is reset by `act` deliberately to disarm a purge, and `message` is never server-seeded — `pending.suggestedMessage` reaches it as a `placeholder` (`:153`), not a value.

**No regression test, and why.** The three precedent tests are prop → `renderToStaticMarkup` → assert. `RunLand` takes only a run and builds the card from a fetch in an effect; static markup runs no effects, so it renders the `!state` branch, which is `null`. Pinning this needs a renderer that runs effects plus a `fetch` stub, and neither jsdom, a testing library nor `react-test-renderer` is a dependency here — a framework, not a test.

**Verification** (exact commands, in order):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev` | ok |
| `npm run typecheck` | passes, no output |
| `npm test` | 585 pass, 0 fail, 82 suites |
| `npm run build` | **fails** — `TypeError: generate is not a function` |
| `env -u __NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG npm run build` | passes, exit 0, compiled in 5.5s |

The build failure is environmental, not the code: it reproduces on a clean tree at HEAD (`git stash` → same error), on `--turbopack`, and with `next.config.ts` replaced by a plain `.js` one. This container inherits `__NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG` from the Next standalone server supervising it; `next build` takes that JSON as its whole config, JSON cannot carry `generateBuildId: () => null`, so `generateBuildId(config.generateBuildId, nanoid)` (`next/dist/build/index.js:358`) gets `undefined` and throws before the banner prints. With the variable unset the build is clean. No browser has rendered the change.

**Closing comment:** https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/48#issuecomment-5284595050

**Noticed, left alone:** `src/app/branches/page.tsx:458` has the identical defect — `load()` sets `strategy` from `json.defaultStrategy` unconditionally, `act()` re-reads after Delete/Commit/Purge (`:554`), and that same `strategy` is what `queueSelected()` sends to the merge queue (`:573`). Same class, different surface, out of scope for this issue.

DONE
